sentences: `spirv/index.json`: one entry per translated shader with its stage, `wave64` / `subgroup_size`, SPIR-V capabilities and extensions, the Vulkan **features** to enable (barycentrics, interlock, mesh, geometry, Float64, Int64, buffer device address, write-without-format, `shaderFmaFloat32` for `--fma khr`, …), `needs_maintenance8`, the descriptor bindings it uses (set 0), push-constant size, `local_size`, `user_sgprs` (CS), `lds_bytes`, mesh `max_vertices`/`max_primitives`/`params`, geometry inputs/outputs, vertex-input locations and types, full `vertex_input_signature` (ISG1 register/mask/system-value/component-type, for PSO lookup), `wave64_emulated` (true for VS/PS/GS wave64, which the translator emits as per-subgroup code with no cross-half exchange, and for compute/mesh translated with `--wave64-emulate`; the runtime does not use it: it reads `wave64`, `subgroup_size` and `wave64_exchange`), `dynamic_format` (runtime V# FORMAT: codes outside FORMATS decode to 0) / `fixed_format_codes`, `src_sha256` and optional `fssm_sha256` (via `--fssm-dir`), PS system inputs, `bary_fallback_input` (`--bary-fallback`: the location of the barycentric input), `mesh_compute` (`--mesh-compute`: the slot layout and push-constant size), `pc_tail` (`--pc-tail-ubo`: the set, binding and size of the uniform block that holds the push-constant tail), and input/output locations.
A shader translated with `--wave64-emulate` carries `wave64_exchange: "workgroup"` and `subgroup_size: null`: any subgroup size is exact, request none.

Otherwise `subgroup_size` (64 for wave64, 32) is what the PSO asks for through `VkPipelineShaderStageRequiredSubgroupSizeCreateInfo` where the device lists the stage in `requiredSubgroupSizeStages` (docs/d3d12_vulkan.md section 3.2): that list is the driver's, not "compute/mesh only".

The AMD Windows driver reports FRAGMENT, COMPUTE, TASK and MESH (measured on a Radeon 880M, driver 26.11.2, sizes 32..64), and current Mesa RADV on GFX10+ reports COMPUTE, FRAGMENT and task/mesh (`src/amd/vulkan/radv_physical_device.c`, `requiredSubgroupSizeStages`, Mesa main at 152b9cde; older Mesa: compute only), so wave64 pixel shaders can run exact there.
NVIDIA lists every stage but only size 32, so there a native wave64 shader cannot get 64 and wave64 PS/VS/GS stay 2x32.
A runtime can create every pipeline at load time from it without parsing SPIR-V.
